argument_summary: The cleanest supportable position on the existing admissible record is narrower than the original packet: the record clearly satisfies the P1, service-link, and scoped-access-insufficiency elements through BACC-028-A, BACC-028-B, and BACC-028-C, and it also shows partial support for the approver predicate through BACC-028-E when read with BACC-028-D. The overbroad claim is that the approver condition is fully established. What the record actually supports is a bounded, caveated compliance judgment: the exception is defensible under the emergency-access policy on a risk-weighted basis, but the approver-unavailability element is not documented as strongly as the other elements because the response-window definition is not in evidence and secondary approver status is unrecorded.
claims_about_policy: Under the policy text in the record, elevated emergency access requires four elements: P1 incident, documented link to the failing service, documented insufficiency of scoped access, and either approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization. The first three are directly supported by admissible evidence. For the fourth, there is no break-glass preauthorization in the record, so the defense must rest on approver unavailability. BACC-028-E does not conclusively prove that approval could not be obtained within the response window, but it is still relevant evidence of unavailability because it documents 18 minutes of primary-approver nonresponse during a live incident and no recorded secondary status. That supports a caveated rather than categorical compliance assessment. The actor withdraws any stronger claim that the policy conditions are fully established without qualification.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is offered as policy support. The relevant point is only that remaining uncertainty appears documentational and bounded, not a sign that the access-service link or least-privilege insufficiency was fabricated or unsupported. That makes monitoring or post-incident documentation follow-up more proportionate than escalation on the present record.
concessions: The original packet overstated the approver element by treating incomplete approver-status evidence as if it fully satisfied the policy requirement.
The record does not define the applicable response window, so it cannot be shown conclusively from current evidence that approval could not be obtained within that window.
The secondary approver path is not affirmatively documented as unavailable; it is only unrecorded.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No reliance is placed on private executive direction or operational urgency alone.
